raw_record.support_text: In Amanita phalloides (amatoxin) poisoning, electrolyte abnormalities should be corrected and liver enzyme levels, INR, and lactate monitored for prognosis; the paper discusses liver transplantation for the resulting severe hepatic injury, noting transplantation should be delayed until 2–4 days after poisoning to allow elimination of amatoxin and prevent graft poisoning. In the authors' case series, four of ten patients with clinically significant poisoning died despite intravenous silibinin and other treatments, and early predictors of severe (potentially fatal) poisoning are discussed.

raw_record.support_text: Reporting adverse events in a prospective single-centre study of 30 febrile neutropenic haematological-malignancy patients receiving teicoplanin loading and maintenance doses (600-800 mg/day), the authors state that nephrotoxicity was observed in five patients (16.7%), but that 'There was no evidence of hepatotoxicity in the study cohort.' No liver injury, hepatotoxicity, or drug-induced liver injury was attributed to teicoplanin in this study.
raw_record.qualifying_conditions: Findings apply to febrile neutropenic patients with haematological malignancy; exposure was therapeutic IV teicoplanin (loading then maintenance 600-800 mg/day).
raw_record.extra_details: Prospective study of 30 patients; teicoplanin generally well tolerated; four patients (13.3%) developed skin rash (all with concurrent potentially rash-causing medications) and one severe hypersensitivity reaction occurred; nephrotoxicity seen in five patients (16.7%), mostly with concurrent nephrotoxic co-medications. Explicit statement: 'There was no evidence of hepatotoxicity in the study cohort.'
